relevance_note: Single-centre cohort of 13 Blau syndrome patients with NOD2 variants, with per-patient supplementary tables: "identified 8 different variants in 13 patients".
method_note: Built with a short Python script (build.py in scratch) that copies table rows verbatim from the paper; every value was chosen by reading the paper, and script spans were checked against the tables. Scope: all 13 cohort patients (P1-P13, labels from Supplementary Tables S1/S2; text also uses 'Patient 1/2/3') carry NOD2 variants; P1 is the mother of P2 (both cohort members). Two relatives are added because S2 attributes the variant to them: father of P3 ('Inherited from Father') and mother of P8 ('Inherited from Mother'); nothing else is reported about them. Variants: only the five non-R334W/R334Q patients in S2 (P3, P6, P8, P9, P10) have printed per-patient variants. The other 8 patients (P1, P2, P4, P5, P7, P11, P12, P13) carry p.R334W (n=6) or p.R334Q (n=2) per Table 1 counts, but the paper never says which patient carries which, so their variant rows have variant_original_string 'not reported'. Transcript NM_022162 is stated once for the whole NOD2 analysis and is applied to every row. Zygosity is not stated for anyone. S2 row P6 has stacked cells ('c.1411C>T, p.R471C; / c.1487A>C, p.H496P', 'Inherited; / de novo', 'Benign ...; / Likely Pathogenic ...'); per D-31 these are not assigned by position, so p.R471C's inheritance and classification are 'not reported'; p.H496P's de novo status and Likely Pathogenic (PM1, PM2, PM5, PP3) come from the Results text. Inheritance for P9 and P10 is left 'not reported' although S2 says 'de novo', because the paper does not state that both parents were tested negative (rule 8); the 'de novo' entries are kept in parental_testing_statement. The P6 ocular cell (glaucoma, cataracts / corneal deformity / phthisis bulbi) is stacked but belongs to one person, so all values are recorded for P6. Group statements used: 'all patients had polyarthritis'/'arthritis developed in all 13' (arthritis observed for all), 'None of the patients showed cardiac, central nervous system, or hearing involvement' (excluded for all 13; cardiac absence used to exclude pericarditis; CNS absence not used for cranial neuropathy), 'All patients were Han Chinese'. Table 1/S3/S4 counts exclude no one. P1 and P4: normal WBC/ESR/CRP are reported only during TNF-inhibitor therapy in remission, so they are recorded as excluded phenotypic_features rows but the lifetime checklist item 'elevated inflammatory markers' is left 'not reported'. P7 is identified as the single canakinumab patient (S1 CANA group n=1; Table 2 Canakinumab Group n=1); text about 'one patient' treated with canakinumab (hepatic comorbidity/TIPS; improvement in arthritis, skin rash, fever) and Table 2's 'Pred added later for ILD' are attributed to P7 on that basis. Not attributed (would require matching patients across tables by regimen): Table 2 footnotes a-c (IFX switch, cost switch, elevated creatinine), primary ADA failure/No Response in the conventional group, the tofacitinib case, the septic shock case, the liver cirrhosis/hepatosplenomegaly patient and the renal, vascular and pulmonary cases. Not recorded as skin rash: P3's erythema nodosum-like nodules (recorded under erythema nodosum/panniculitis) and P8's keratosis pilaris. Ages: only diagnostic delays (P1 25 years, P2 7 years) are given per patient; no ages. Publication: cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is set true from 'our previous study [21]' plus 'expanded pedigrees in the current analysis', which implies but does not explicitly state overlap. Supplementary Fig. 1 (pedigrees) is images only. No contradictions found.
